proseChanges.summary: **Delta import lease lapses:** every lease-guarded batch now reports a lost workspace lease, including run initialization, replay bookkeeping and completion. A lapse stops the import; already committed progress stays journaled and replay can complete without duplicating it. Unrelated batch failures retain their original error. This fixes the slow-tier legacy-export failure that prevented v0.4.23 from being pinned by the platform. **First-owner legacy adoption:** Move in now uses importer v2 for new original HappyToHelp packages. The original native installation owner reviews the setup and source workspace IDs and explicitly approves the exact package fingerprint with a recent sign-in proof. Bounded preflight then creates the source ID as a separate historical workspace; the setup workspace, native accounts and Business link stay intact. Only the approving owner gains membership. Missing original-owner binding refuses adoption; an older installation cannot infer that authority from matching account details. Imported AI profiles remain disabled and system workflows stay draft. Historical source people, matching email addresses and old roles grant no sign-in, membership or assignment authority. An existing destination without this package's adoption provenance conflicts. Upload alone starts no import; Stop and Resume retain committed history. **Private source custody and erasure:** v2 registers source originals and scratch privately with bounded retention: upload, paused, stopped and completed-source windows are at most 24 hours, with progress bounded by seven days from first admission. Polling does not extend retention. Contact erasure or workspace deletion fences the whole package across its setup, source and destination scopes, including before start; cleanup continues without the importing session or an active workspace. Failed cleanup remains pending, closure of the same fingerprint is terminal, and erasure blocks fresh packages in that scope. Canonical history for other contacts remains. Results distinguish historical verification from current source availability; source originals confer no download entitlement. **Historical readers and old synthetic packages:** imported note buckets, assignment attribution and macro creator snapshots display as history; historical people stay out of native member and assignment lists. Existing v1 artifacts remain synthetic and cannot become v2 adoption by updating the Worker. Bounded old-prefix discovery and cleanup seeding register coordinates before purging source and scratch; native erasure stays pending until discovery, seeding and purge finish. The original installation owner can explicitly close a known v1 package through the protected cleanup API. Missing or unreadable inventory is pending cleanup. New native setup records a private counts-only installation baseline; an older installation keeps an unavailable baseline rather than inventing one. Installation-wide diagnostics remain restricted to the original owner. **Fresh hosted installs and retained delivery:** native setup and ordinary support remain active. The importer runner and adoption are inert until a legacy package is imported through the approved flow; installing these tables starts no import, sends no mail and grants no historical user access. This release retains v0.4.23's corrected mail declaration and rer 0.2.112, including native off / own / rer mail choices and explicit MAIL_PROVIDER=none/disabled taking precedence. It does not newly introduce those mail changes. Real customer remote importer use still requires separate combined ordering, restart and browser qualification plus signed migration-before-Worker delivery. Hosted live-provider qualification and importer follow-up refinements remain separate; this release does not authorize a production import or cutover. **Migrations:** four since v0.4.23, applied once in filename order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic: `328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql`, `329_legacy_package_custody.sql`, `331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql`, then `332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql`. Stop the old Worker and back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. 328 adds adoption, mapping and actor-origin tables plus a nullable note bucket column; 329 adds private custody, key-ledger and scope-fence tables/indexes; 331 adds cleanup columns, seed/inventory/baseline tables and an index, and inserts an inventory marker. These are additive schema changes. 332 is a conditional data cleanup, not additive-only: it deletes just the unstarted empty inventory marker when no package custody or import run exists, preserving existing cursors and package/run inventory. No source history, account or permission is rewritten. There is no 330 file (reserved for platform recovery); 326 is also absent. The complete inventory is 195 migration files. Upgrade order is v0.4.23 -> v0.4.24; v0.4.22 first applies 327 and v0.4.21 first applies 324 and 325, retaining their published buyer steps.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.23 carries the corrected mail declaration and rer 0.2.112 with 191 migrations; its slow-tier legacy-export run failed and the platform refused to pin it.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.24 fixes delta lease-lapse reporting and carries importer v2 adoption, custody/erasure, historical readers and v1 cleanup seeding. It adds 328, 329, 331 and 332 for 195 migrations; upgrade baselines are v0.4.23, v0.4.22 and v0.4.21. The rer pin remains 0.2.112.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.23 without resetting; v0.4.22 and v0.4.21 are also upgrade baselines. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings, then stop the old Worker. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. Apply 328_legacy_workspace_adoption.sql, 329_legacy_package_custody.sql, 331_legacy_cleanup_seeding.sql and 332_legacy_cleanup_inventory_lazy.sql once in that order BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. A v0.4.22 installation first applies 327_legacy_import_worker.sql; a v0.4.21 installation first applies 324_scheduler_outbox_reads.sql, then 325_knowledge_documents_version_url.sql, then 327, with their published buyer steps. Earlier installations first apply every other missing published migration in filename order. There is no migration 326 or 330 in this release. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. V1 source is cleanup-only and must never be relabeled v2; missing or incomplete cleanup remains pending. No reset, mail activation, recovery adoption, production import, cutover or production deployment is part of this preparation.

migrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings. Apply all missing published migrations in order, then 327 and 328 once BEFORE the v2 Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. Additive adoption reservations, provenance, explicit historical mapping profile and actor origins; preserves native accounts, setup workspace and Business binding. No reset, mail activation or cutover. Release v0.4.24: upgrade from v0.4.23 in order 328, 329, 331, 332; 330 has no file. Keep the old Worker stopped until all missing migrations finish. Retain every applied identity; do not reapply 327. V0.4.22 first applies 327; v0.4.21 first applies 324, 325, 327 with their published steps. No reset or production import authorized.

Keep original synthetic v1 sources separate and cleanup-only; do not relabel them v2 or admit real customer sources before independent qualification. No reset or deployment authorized. Old synthetic manifest/prefix coordinates are registered pagewise before bounded purge; erasure remains pending until inventory and seeding complete. No reset or customer enablement. pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1, R2 and private installation encryption custody before updating. Apply 330_identity_recovery.sql once BEFORE the new Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. On v0.4.24, apply this missing filename even though 331 and 332 are already recorded; retain every applied migration identity. Keep the durable recovery revocation watermark on rollback. Discard live recovery requests, approvals, pending factors and capabilities on restore; rebind Managed custody after a portable restore. This adds scoped first-owner and all-workspace consent recovery state and invalidation triggers without rewriting accounts, factors, memberships or spent-key history. Managed recovery remains unavailable until the separate declaration and custody round enables it. No reset or deployment is authorized.
